resolved.title: #ifdef，#ifndef 和 #undef 指令
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]The #ifdef, #ifndef, and #undef Directives[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

The [b]#ifdef[/b], [b]#ifndef[/b], and [b]#undef[/b] directives operate on macros created with [b]#define[/b]. 
For example, there will be compilation problems if the same macro is defined twice, so you can check for this with an [b]#ifdef[/b] directive. Or if you may want to redefine a macro, you first use [b]#undef[/b].

The program below demonstrates these directives:[code format="c" codeId="2216"]#include <stdio.h>

#define RATE 0.08
[b]#ifndef TERM[/b]
  #define TERM 24
[b]#endif[/b]

int main() {
  [b]#ifdef[/b] RATE  /* this branch will be compiled */
    [b]#undef[/b] RATE  
    printf("Redefining RATE\n");
    #define RATE 0.068
  [b]#else[/b]  /* this branch will not be compiled */
    #define RATE 0.068
  [b]#endif[/b]

  printf("%f  %d\n", RATE, TERM);

  return 0;
} [/code]
Because RATE is defined at the top, only the #ifdef clause will be compiled. The optional #else branch compiles when #ifdef RATE is false during preprocessing. 
An [b]#endif[/b] is required to close the block of code.
[note]An [b]#elif[/b] directive is like an else if and can be used to provide additional alternatives after #else.[/note]

content.text: `#if`和`if`语句是不能互换的。`#if`使用预处理器可用的数据进行评估，然后只发送真正的分支代码进行编译。

The #if and if statement are not interchangeable. The #if is evaluated using data available to the preprocessor, which then sends only the true branch for compilation.

#if和if语句是不能互换的。#if使用预处理器可用的数据进行评估，然后只发送真正的分支进行编译。

content.text: 一个`if`语句使用在运行时提供数据，并有可能分支到任何`else`子句。
